name: Entity Reference Edit Link
description: Adds an 'Edit' link beside the referenced entity inside entity reference field widgets on entity edit forms, shown only when the current user has update access to that entity.

suggests.drupal/select2: Optional. If the Select2 module is installed and a field uses the 'select2_entity_reference' widget, the module also adds the edit link to that widget (a single link for single-value fields, a dropbutton of links for multi-value fields).

provides_plugin_types.note: Not a new widget plugin ID. hook_field_widget_info_alter() swaps core's 'entity_reference_autocomplete' widget class for this subclass of EntityReferenceAutocompleteWidget, which adds a per-delta '_link' edit link when the referenced entity has an 'edit-form' link template and the current user passes an 'update' access check.
Subclass of EntityReferenceAutocompleteTagsWidget swapped in via hook_field_widget_info_alter(); it explicitly unsets the '_link' element so the tags (comma-separated) widget shows no edit link.

project_description: The module should be useful for content editors because it allows them to easily navigate to the entity that is used as an entity reference. It adds an 'Edit' link to the referenced entity inside entity reference field widgets (the core entity_reference_autocomplete widget, and, when installed, the Select2 select2_entity_reference widget) on entity edit forms. The link is rendered only when the referenced entity exposes an 'edit-form' link template AND the current user has 'update' access to that entity; links open in a new browser tab (target=_blank). For multi-value autocomplete fields the link is shown in an added 'Edit Entity' table column; for multi-value Select2 fields the links are grouped in a dropbutton. The tags (comma-separated) autocomplete widget is deliberately excluded. Separately, from version 1.1.0, a configuration page at /admin/config/entity-reference-edit-link (permission: administer site configuration) lets an administrator select content types for which the node edit page title gains an 'Edit <type>' link pointing to that content type's Manage fields (Field UI) page; that title link is only shown to users holding the 'administer node fields' permission.
